RATE_CONTRAST_observation: Your key points go by as fast as the setup around them.
RATE_CONTRAST_why_it_matters: Slowing down on what matters tells the listener what to focus on.
RATE_CONTRAST_practice: Slow down on the point, then move through the setup.
RATE_IMPORTANCE_FAST_why_it_matters: A little more time can make this passage easier to follow.
RATE_IMPORTANCE_FAST_practice: Give this phrase a little more time, then resume your natural pace.
RATE_IMPORTANCE_SLOW_why_it_matters: A brisker pace can help this passage keep its momentum.
RATE_IMPORTANCE_SLOW_practice: Move through this phrase more briskly and save time for the key idea.
PAUSE_NECESSARY_observation: This stretch runs on without a pause.
PAUSE_NECESSARY_why_it_matters: A pause gives the listener a moment to take in what you just said.
PAUSE_NECESSARY_practice: Stop at the marked place and let the point land before you go on.
PAUSE_TOO_SHORT_why_it_matters: The point needs a moment to sink in before you move on.
PAUSE_TOO_SHORT_practice: Hold the marked pause longer and let the point land.
PAUSE_UNNECESSARY_observation: The pauses here break up the thought.
PAUSE_UNNECESSARY_why_it_matters: Stopping every few words makes one idea hard to follow.
PAUSE_UNNECESSARY_practice: Say this thought in one breath, without stopping at the marked places.
PAUSE_TOO_LONG_observation: This silence goes on too long.
PAUSE_TOO_LONG_why_it_matters: A silence this long stops sounding deliberate, and the listener starts to wonder if you lost your place.
PAUSE_TOO_LONG_practice: Keep the pause, but move on after a beat or two.
VOLUME_LOW_observation: Your voice drops here and loses its projection.
VOLUME_LOW_why_it_matters: Volume carries confidence and energy; when it drops, listeners have to work to stay with you.
VOLUME_LOW_practice: Keep the volume you use elsewhere through this stretch, about a 6 or 7 out of 10.
VOLUME_FADE_observation: Your voice trails off at the end of these sentences.
VOLUME_FADE_why_it_matters: The end of a sentence often carries the point; when it fades, it gets lost.
VOLUME_FADE_practice: Take a breath at the pause before, and carry your volume through to the last word.
PITCH_VARIETY_observation: Your voice stays on one note through this stretch.
PITCH_VARIETY_why_it_matters: Melody tells listeners what matters and makes it easier to remember; a voice on one note is easy to tune out.
PITCH_VARIETY_practice: Say it again and let your voice move: lift the word that matters, then let it fall. To widen your range, read a page while sliding slowly from low to high and back.
PITCH_HIGH_observation: Your voice sits much higher here than in the rest of your talk.
PITCH_HIGH_why_it_matters: A voice stuck high draws attention to itself and away from your message.
PITCH_HIGH_practice: Say it again in your usual speaking voice, and let it rise only on the words that matter.
PITCH_LOW_observation: Your voice drops much lower here than in the rest of your talk.
PITCH_LOW_why_it_matters: Stuck low, your voice loses its energy, and listeners notice the drop more than the message.
PITCH_LOW_practice: Say it again in your usual speaking voice and let it move: lift the word that matters, then let it fall.
TONE_FLAT_why_it_matters: Listeners connect with the feeling in your voice, not only with the words.
TONE_FLAT_practice: Decide what this passage should feel like, let your face show it, and say it again.
RATE_SLOWS_FOR_POINT_why_it_matters: Slowing down on what matters is a verbal highlight: it tells the listener this is the part to focus on.
RATE_SLOWS_FOR_POINT_practice: Keep this. In your next take, find the line that matters most and give it the same room.
PAUSE_LETS_IT_LAND_why_it_matters: The silence gives the listener time to process the point before you move on.
PAUSE_LETS_IT_LAND_practice: Keep this pause. Give your next key point the same beat.
PAUSE_BUILDS_ANTICIPATION_why_it_matters: Holding back what comes next makes the listener lean in for it.
PAUSE_BUILDS_ANTICIPATION_practice: Keep it. Try the same pause before your next answer or reveal.
TONE_EXPRESSIVE_why_it_matters: Listeners connect with the feeling in your voice, not only with the words; here they can hear that you mean it.
TONE_EXPRESSIVE_practice: Keep this. Notice what your face is doing here, and bring it to the flatter passages.
PITCH_MELODY_why_it_matters: Melody tells listeners what matters and makes your message easier to remember, the way a song is.
PITCH_MELODY_practice: Keep this range, and bring the same movement to the stretches where your voice settles on one note.
PITCH_MELODY_observation: Your voice moves freely between high and low notes through this stretch.
